I have a large plot of 13.40 hectares here in Dar es Salaam region, which I intercrop with cassava, sweet potato, and coconut to feed my family and sell in the city market. Chemical fertilizer is too expensive and hard to find here on the coast, so I do not use it, but I do spread manure from my livestock to improve the sandy soil. We work this land mostly with family labor using hand hoes, though I hire some workers during the busy weeding and harvest seasons. I plant the seeds I have saved from previous seasons because they do well in our local conditions, and I rely on the rains since we cannot irrigate such a big plot.
